subject: Food Science
title: Toxin-Producing Organisms
description: Learn Toxin-Producing Organisms in one minute.

hook.text: Staphylococcus aureus toxin causes vomiting within hours of eating. Reheating the food doesn't help—the toxin is heat stable.

buildup.text: Some bacteria produce toxins in food before you eat it. The bacteria can be killed, but the toxin remains active.

discovery.text: Bacillus cereus in cooked rice produces cereulide toxin at room temperature. Reheated rice can cause severe vomiting.

twist.text: Fried rice syndrome—B. cereus from leftover rice—sends thousands to hospitals yearly. The fix: refrigerate rice within an hour.

climax.text: Aflatoxin from Aspergillus mold is the most potent liver carcinogen known. It contaminates 25% of the world's grain supply.

punchline.text: Kill the bacteria and the toxin stays. Prevention beats treatment every time.

quiz.question: Why doesn't reheating fix Staphylococcus toxin in food?
options: The toxin is heat-stable and remains active even after bacteria die
